summary.text: Animated multispectral satellite imagery (MSI) depicts persistent, deep convection concentrated along the western periphery of an elongated low-level circulation center (LLCC). Recent scatterometer data indicate that TS 26W has accelerated west-northwestward, with an average forward speed of 14 kt during the past 12 hours. Toward +24h, a progressive shortwave trough racing downstream of northern Honshu and Hokkaido will erode the STR, resulting in a marked weakening of the primary steering influence and causing TS 26W to become nearly stationary.

summary.text: Animated multispectral satellite imagery (MSI) depicts tropical storm (TS) 26W (choi-wan) improving in structure with a more symmetrical and partially obscured low level circulation center (LLCC). TS 26W has slowed in track speed and begun a poleward turn as it enters an area of weaker steering influence as a shortwave trough to the north propagates eastward, weakening the western extension of the subtropical ridge (STR) centered to the northeast. Regarding intensity, 26W is forecast to continue intensifying out to a peak of 105 kt between taus 48 and 60, with a period of rapid intensification (ri) explicitly forecast from +12h to 36 as 26W gains a poleward outflow channel and VWS continues to abate.

summary.text: Animated enhanced infrared (EIR) satellite imagery depicts typhoon 26W (choi-wan) with a compact inner-core and an intermittent eye that has been cycling over the past 6 hours.
